meta.description: Actionable tasks for dev agents. Created during deep-dive analysis. Each task has: repo, priority, acceptance criteria, and context. Dev agents: pick up tasks in priority order, create a branch, work, PR back. The atlas agent will review 12hrs after your work fires.
meta.flow: Atlas agent reviews repos → creates tasks → 12hrs later dev agents execute → 12hrs later atlas agent reviews and adds more

tasks.title: Split schedule.tsx (60KB) into focused components
tasks.context: artifacts/mobile/app/(tabs)/schedule.tsx is 60KB — a single file containing the weekly grid, the host-a-run modal, court search field, day/time pickers, and all scheduling logic. This is unmaintainable and blocks safe iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Extract CourtField (court search/select) into components/schedule/CourtField.tsx
Extract DayTimeGrid into components/schedule/DayTimeGrid.tsx
Extract HostRunModal into components/schedule/HostRunModal.tsx
Extract VisitModal into components/schedule/VisitModal.tsx
schedule.tsx imports the extracted components and is under 15KB
All existing functionality preserved — no behavior changes
TypeScript compiles clean (pnpm tsc --noEmit)

tasks.title: Fix Add Friend button (broken in build 9)
tasks.context: SCREEN_MAP.md documents: 'Add Friend does nothing in build 9; it previously worked.' The button exists on the player profile screen (artifacts/mobile/app/player/[id].tsx) but the friendshipService.ts call appears to not fire or fails silently. This blocks the core social loop.
acceptance_criteria: Identify why Add Friend fails — check friendshipService.createFriendRequest, RLS policies, and error handling
Fix the root cause (not just surface symptom)
Add a loading state on the button while the request is pending
Add error toast on failure
Add success feedback (either toast or button state change to 'Requested')
Test with two real accounts if possible, or document the RLS verification needed

tasks.title: Map UI cleanup — remove redundant controls per Jesse's annotations
tasks.context: Screenshot 18-map-layout-annotations.png shows Jesse's working direction: retain shared Explore header, make List/Map the primary view switch, remove redundant banner, legend, and floating add affordances. The map currently has competing UI elements that reduce clarity.
acceptance_criteria: Remove redundant banner from MapScreen
Remove floating legend that competes with map content
Remove floating add-court button (move to header or Explore list)
List/Map becomes a segmented toggle in the Explore header
Empty state (screenshot 19) keeps Explore context visible
No layout overflow on iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone SE

tasks.title: Resolve Issue #18 Part A: Remove obsolete MAPBOX_DOWNLOADS_TOKEN config
tasks.context: Issue #18 states @rnmapbox/maps@10.3.2 does NOT require a Mapbox downloads secret. But app.config.js still references RNMAPBOX_MAPS_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN and comments say it's required for builds. This is contradictory and will confuse the EAS build.
acceptance_criteria: Remove RNMAPBOX_MAPS_DOWNLOAD_TOKEN references from app.config.js
Update comments to clarify only EXPO_PUBLIC_MAPBOX_TOKEN (pk.*) is needed
Check .env.example for stale MAPBOX_DOWNLOADS_TOKEN references
Check EAS environment variables documentation
Verify no CI/build scripts reference the download token

tasks.title: Add MCP tools: create_instruction, update_instruction, delete_instruction
tasks.context: The MCP function (supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts) only exposes 3 read-only tools: list_groups, list_instructions, get_production_instruction. An agent connected via MCP cannot create or modify instructions — it can only read. This severely limits the product's value proposition of 'version-controlled instructions managed by agents'.
acceptance_criteria: Add create_instruction tool — creates a new instruction_groups row + first version
Add update_instruction tool — creates a new instruction_versions row (never mutates existing versions)
Add delete_instruction tool — soft delete (set archived=true), not a hard delete
All new tools require authentication (ctx.isAuthenticated())
All new tools use user-scoped Supabase client (not service role)
Add Zod input validation matching the DB schema
Update src/lib/mcp/index.ts (the source file — the function is auto-generated from it)

tasks.title: Add health check endpoint + Telegram webhook resilience
tasks.context: The Telegram webhook (supabase/functions/telegram-webhook/index.ts) has no retry logic, no idempotency guard, and errors are silently caught. If Firecrawl or the AI gateway fails, the thread is lost. There's also no health endpoint to verify the service is alive.
acceptance_criteria: Add idempotency: store telegram update_id in a processed_updates table, skip duplicates
Add retry with exponential backoff for Firecrawl scrape failures (max 3 retries)
If classification fails, still save the thread with group_id=null and rating=null (don't lose data)
Add a /health endpoint to the MCP function that returns {status: 'ok', timestamp}
Log structured errors to Supabase (an error_logs table or similar)
Telegram send failures should not crash the webhook — catch and log

tasks.title: RLS audit — verify all tables have correct policies
tasks.context: 6 migrations exist but there's no evidence RLS policies were verified. The MCP tools use user-scoped Supabase clients, but if RLS is missing or permissive, any authenticated user could read/modify other users' instructions. This is a security gate before any public deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Read all 6 migration files and document every table + its RLS policies
For each table, verify: (a) RLS is enabled, (b) SELECT policies restrict to own rows, (c) INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE restrict to own rows
List any tables with missing or permissive policies
Create a migration to fix any gaps
Document the expected RLS policy for each table in a SECURITY.md or similar
